source_episode_contract.source: Incoming source sessions serve continuously before/during initial copy; pause at actual request boundary, wait in-flight completion, catch up actual retained state, commit ownership, retain scheduled queue.
source_episode_contract.control: Incoming state materialized before episode and mirrored after source completions, tagged control_materialization; resulting extra destination baseline work must be reported separately. Baseline contention is not assumed equivalent to replay/KV. Mirroring currently holds the source session dependency lock, so source send lateness and state at migration may differ despite identical offered arrivals; report this explicitly.
source_episode_contract.service_probe_deviation: Actual full retained token history uses completion token-ID path for service migration, max_tokens512 with normal EOS; serving turns retain recorded fixed output lengths and actual generated tokens. This differs from original chat probe and validates token input/hash/generation continuity, not semantic state-code recall. Controlled KV diagnostics retain original full-message chat probe512.
source_episode_contract.recovery: Continuing arrivals through300; outstanding at migration+30/+120 and each later window relative to matched control. Cleanup drain never proves recovery.
source_episode_contract.cache_isolation: Before each episode, verify both engines idle, then clear owned source/destination MP L1 cache, owned Redis storage and native prefix caches. Service requests use no cache_salt because existing explicit MP prefetch does not pass it; interepisode cleanup isolates matched content and memory. Never clear during baseline/measurement or between initial copy and catch-up; native prefix reuse preserved.
source_episode_contract.incoming_rate_basis: Existing simulator source_session_rps per physical session; actual offered/completed RPS measured separately, no capacity percentage claim.

east_server_observations.scope: Existing complete local server joins, grouped by offered-arrival window; full observed generation may finish after the window. Server intervals share verified local clocks. No Germany/East clock subtraction or client-derived GPU iteration time.

scope: One measured source GPU and one destination GPU per episode; all twenty Germany episodes, including eight resident-only scouts, remain present.

Arrival-window latency uses observations through the fixed episode boundary; window-end coverage is separately retained. Unfinished and undispatched arrivals remain in denominators. Known violation counts include right-censored TTFT lower bounds; failed/dependency-failed requests with no first token remain separate failures, not latency observations through the boundary.

Completed-request throughput counts successful response completion events in each interval. Output-token credit is assigned at response completion and is not a token-delivery rate or exclusive GPU work.

Outstanding counts unresolved offered service obligations. Explicit client failures and requests censored at the observation cutoff remain separate counts; neither is classified as a known live server request, and censoring does not establish terminal server execution. Client pending dispatch and predecessor blocking are distinct from sampled all-population engine running/waiting; client-after-first does not identify exclusive GPU decode activity.

Finite handoff-cohort clearance excludes later arrivals. First empty resident state and the end of a matched completion deficit do not prove stationary recovery or a window SLO. Cleanup after the boundary is not recovery.

Controls share offered resident shapes and arrivals but perform recorded destination mirroring; actual incoming source evolution can differ. Comparisons describe measured outcomes, not isolated pure migration causality.
Client mean TPOT can contain buffered token delivery; only the separate East server-ready intervals diagnose server generation cadence.

The current fleet starts resident fluid debt at zero, creates debt only during migration compute, and drains it using average headroom. That state cannot encode already-active requests, serialized pending turns, individual first-token deadlines or delayed long output completions. Clearing this scalar by D does not certify the posted P90 TTFT or TPOT targets.
